title: Seeding & Determinism Contracts for Hosted Generation (PRD + Launch Checklist)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a clear, auditable contract for deterministic/seeding behavior across Redwood hosted endpoints (chat, completions, rerank, embeddings where applicable). Objective is to offer customers a documented, supported way to reproduce outputs for debugging, audits, and evaluation while maintaining safe and performant serving. This PRD defines the API surface changes, runtime requirements, cross-endpoint semantics, non-goals, and a gated launch checklist including tests, canaries, docs, and SDK updates.
non_goals: Make all model variants bitwise-identical across hardware — that remains out of scope (we will document expected variance with quantized kernels).
Guarantee determinism across model architecture changes or new checkpoints — only guaranteed for pinned model versions and runtime profile combos.
Force seeding semantics on embeddings by default — embeddings stability is handled separately (see embedding stability guardrail item).
requirements: API: Add optional integer query parameter/JSON field 'seed' (32-bit signed) accepted by chat/completions/rerank endpoints; when provided, server must use seed to drive sampling RNG deterministically for that request.

API: Document clear precedence/interaction between 'seed' and other sampling params (temperature, top_p, n, top_k); identical set of params + seed + model + runtime profile => reproducible token sequence.
Streaming: For streaming responses, streamed token sequence must match the non-streaming full-result when the same seed is used (no reordering or additional tokens).

Function calling: When function-calling is enabled, selection of function and ordered arguments must be reproducible given the same seed; non-deterministic external side-effects remain outside contract.
Rerank: For rerank endpoints, seed must deterministically affect stochastic tie-breaking and sampling-based rerankers. When seed omitted, existing stochastic behavior retained.

Embeddings: 'seed' is ignored for embeddings endpoint; instead, provide an optional 'embed-stability-level' flag (low/medium/high) and document tradeoffs; require stability tests across quantization modes.

Runtime: Runtime must expose a seeded RNG that is resilient to batching — different requests with same seed must produce identical outputs regardless of batching boundaries or concurrent traffic (i.e., RNG draws must be request-scoped).

Compatibility: Guarantee provided only for pinned model versions and documented runtime kernel combinations; changing model or runtime invalidates the reproducibility guarantee and must surface a clear warning in responses/headers and docs.

Telemetry: Surface a header 'X-Seed-Applied' when a seed is honored and 'X-Determinism-Warning' when determinism cannot be guaranteed (e.g., fallback to different model variant or quantization mismatch).
Docs & SDKs: Provide examples in HTTP/REST, Python, and TypeScript SDKs including streaming examples, function call examples, and a reproducibility debugging guide.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/integration tests: For each supported model + runtime profile (min matrix: 2 model families x 2 kernel profiles), run 200 deterministic sampling tests where identical seed+params produce identical token sequences for chat and completions (>= 99.5% pass rate).
Streaming parity: End-to-end test asserts that streaming and non-streaming outputs are byte-identical when same seed is used (100% pass for test matrix).
Rerank consistency: For a canonical rerank workload, seeded reranks must produce identical ranking orders and score vectors across 100 seeded trials (>= 99.5% pass).

Embedding stability: Embedding stability harness reports cosine variance <= 0.002 across a representative set of 1000 queries for 'high' stability mode on supported runtime profiles. (This requirement gated — if not achievable for a runtime, mark as 'unsupported' in docs and expose in header).

SDKs: Python and TypeScript SDKs include seed parameter in function signatures, streaming helper that exposes seed verification, and unit tests demonstrating reproducibility. PRs merged and released to npm/pypi pre-launch.
Docs: Confluence spec + public docs page with clear examples, migration guidance, and determinism caveats. Docs reviewed by legal for audit language.
Monitoring & Alerts: Production dashboards with metrics described below are live and alerting on drift thresholds (see rollout checklist).
Canary: Canary fleet (1% traffic) must run for 72h with no user-facing regressions and drift_rate metric below threshold (<= 0.5%).
rollout_checklist: API design review completed and OpenAPI patch approved (design review link in 'links').
Runtime: Implement request-scoped seeded RNG and add deterministic draw unit tests (ENG sign-off).
SDK: Python and TS wrappers updated + integration tests against canary endpoint (release branches created).
E2E tests: Add reproducibility CI job that runs nightly against a pinned model+runtime matrix.
Docs: Public docs page draft + internal reproducibility playbook published. Legal & compliance review completed.
Telemetry: Add 'X-Seed-Applied' and 'X-Determinism-Warning' headers; verify headers appear in SDK responses.
Canary plan: 1% of traffic slice for 72h, with automatic rollback on thresholds (drift_rate > 0.5% or increase in 95th latency > 10%).
Monitoring: Create dashboard widgets for 'drift_rate', 'seeded_error_rate', 'seed_vs_unseed_variance', and 'seed-header-ratio'.
Incident Runbook: Add deterministic-related runbook entries (how to retract seed honoring, force fallback, or pin to non-seeded variant).
Release notes & migration guide published; notify top customers with early opt-in window.
monitoring_metrics: drift_rate: fraction of seeded requests that, when re-run in a controlled harness, differ from original output — gate <= 0.5% during canary.
seeded_error_rate: request errors for seeded requests vs baseline — alert if +0.3% above baseline.
seed_header_ratio: proportion of requests that include seed and receive X-Seed-Applied header — used to validate instrumentation.
response_variation_score: normalized token-level difference metric between runs (target <= 0.05 for seeded), computed in nightly CI.
open_risks: Hardware/kernel-level nondeterminism: quantized kernels and GPU scheduling can introduce tiny differences — will require documented unsupported kernel combos or stronger test coverage.
Batching interactions: ensuring request-scoped RNG does not cause performance regressions under heavy batching (tradeoff between isolation and throughput).
Customer expectations: customers may expect cross-model-version reproducibility; must clearly signal scope to avoid support burden.
Function calling side-effects: deterministic selection of function arguments does not guarantee idempotent side-effects; we must clearly document limitations.
decisions: Contract: Seeding is opt-in and request-scoped; default behavior unchanged.
Embeddings: seed ignored by embeddings endpoint; instead offer stability levels. This avoids conflating sampling RNG with deterministic encoder internals.
Telemetry headers: Add X-Seed-Applied and X-Determinism-Warning to surface enforcement and caveats to clients.
Gating: Launch behind a customer-opt-in toggle and then canary to general availability after metrics pass.
